title: Hearing loss in adults: assessment and communication
intro: Hearing loss can make conversation, work and warning sounds harder to follow. It may develop gradually or suddenly and affect one or both ears. Deafness does not indicate intelligence, and communication preferences vary.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Causes include wax, middle-ear problems, noise exposure, aging and inner-ear or nerve conditions. Increasing television volume or struggling in background noise may be early signs; do not assume every change is simply aging.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Assessment includes an ear examination and hearing tests, with further investigation for asymmetric or unusual findings. Explain onset, tinnitus, dizziness, medicines and noise exposure. Online hearing checks cannot exclude urgent causes. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Treatable blockages or infections need suitable care. Hearing aids, assistive devices or selected implant assessment may help permanent loss. Rehabilitation includes fitting, practice and adjustments, not simply buying the loudest device. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Face the person, reduce background noise and speak clearly without shouting. Use captions, written information or sign-language interpretation according to preference. Ask about workplace and healthcare access rather than expecting lipreading to solve everything. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Sudden hearing loss needs urgent same-day assessment, especially in one ear; do not wait for a routine aid appointment or assume wax. Facial weakness, severe dizziness or neurological symptoms require immediate urgent help.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira misses words in meetings and arranges hearing assessment. She also requests captions and quieter seating while exploring suitable devices.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben wakes with markedly reduced hearing in one ear. He seeks urgent assessment rather than trying ear drops for several days.
